A thoughtful approach to AI readiness, learning and responsible innovation across churches and Christian ministries.

Join the waitlist

Ministry AI 360 is currently in development, with an anticipated public rollout in early 2027.

The challenge

Your people are already using AI. Is your ministry ready?

Staff draft sermons with it. Volunteers answer messages with it. Members ask it about faith. Decisions are being made, often without a shared conversation.

Ministries need a calm, biblically grounded way to understand where they stand, learn together and adopt tools wisely, rather than reacting one tool at a time.

Our approach

Ministry AI 360 helps ministries see the whole picture.

It combines a readiness reflection across 16 domains with learning, practical resources and guided support, so a leadership team can start from where it actually is.

  • TeachBuild shared understanding of what AI is, what it is not, and what it means for ministry.
  • EquipGive leaders practical resources, policies and workflows they can adapt.
  • AccompanyWalk alongside ministries as they adopt, review and adjust over time.

The ministry framework

Every part of ministry has a role to play in the age of AI.

From preparing sermons and supporting discipleship to managing finances, communications, and safeguarding people, AI is changing how ministry teams work. Explore 16 areas where thoughtful AI adoption can help ministries work more effectively, while keeping people, wisdom, and spiritual responsibility at the center.

16 areas of ministry. One clearer path to AI readiness.

I am interested in

Questions, answered plainly.

When does Ministry AI 360 launch?

It is in development, with an anticipated public rollout in early 2027. No exact date has been set.

Can I use the platform today?

Not yet. The current application is a demonstration with sample content and no user accounts.

What happens to my details?

Registration is not open yet. When it opens, details will be handled under the privacy notice we publish, and member emails will never appear in the public directory.

Does joining mean I represent my church?

No. Joining only associates you with a church for planning. Official representation is not implied.

Is a church listing public?

Only after approval, and only with an aggregate count.
